assertions.assertion: Its statement of the problem names what decides the right payment (litres with the meter unit converted, at the co-op rate; the month by the dairy's local time) and says the paid or stated amount can differ, so one pickup or farm-month could confirm or refute it
assertions.evidence: There is no separate problem statement. The write-up starts with "the cause is two separate bugs in `milk.py`." The deciding rules (1 gal = 3.785 L; a pickup belongs to its month at the dairy, UTC-7) appear only inside the "Cause:" bullets, as support for the code defects. They are never stated as what decides the right payment.

assertions.assertion: The problem statement does not build in a cause or fix (e.g. 'unit column is ignored', 'month taken from UTC date')
assertions.evidence: The framing is the cause itself: "`pickup_payment` … ignores the `unit` column" and "`month_of` … takes the month straight from the UTC timestamp". No neutral statement is given apart from these causes. The fixes ("Convert gallons… shift UTC by -7 hours") follow directly.

assertions.assertion: Both complaints fit the statement (as one or two problems), and the statement can fail: some named result would show it false
assertions.evidence: Each complaint gets its own section with checkable results: 80 × 3.785 × 0.42 = 127.18 for P-8835, and P-8830 at 2026-10-01T02:40Z is 19:40 on 30 September, so 367.50 + 113.40 = 480.90. A different result from either check would show the claim false.
